**7B.3 Research Note: Abdel Fattah el-Sisi in 2024**

**Bottom line:** The public record gives some evidence of reform intent and a few rule-based programs, but the stronger pattern is continued state favor toward military-connected and other regime-linked actors. I found no reliable public evidence in the sources I searched of a clean separation between Sisi’s personal/family interests and state decisions.

- **[Egypt: Staff and Authorities Reach Agreement on Reviews Under the Extended Fund Facility Arrangement](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/03/06/pr-2459-egypt-staff-and-authorities-reach-agreement-on-reviews-under-the-eff-arrangement)**, IMF, 2024-03-06. Claim: The IMF says the program included a flexible exchange rate, tighter macro policy, and reforms to remove preferential treatment for state-owned enterprises; this is strong evidence of policy intent to reduce connected-actor privilege. Question IDs: 7B.3.

- **[World Bank Group Statement of Support to Egypt’s Development and Reform Efforts](https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/statement/2024/03/18/world-bank-group-statement-of-support-to-egypt-s-development-and-reform-efforts)**, World Bank Group, 2024-03-18. Claim: The Bank framed Egypt’s 2024 agenda around private-sector growth, stronger SOE governance, asset monetization, and a level playing field, which supports a limited pro-separation reading at the level of stated policy. Question IDs: 7B.3.

- **[Arab Republic of Egypt: Technical Assistance Report - Public Investment Management Assessment](https://www.imf.org/en/publications/technical-assistance-reports/issues/2024/04/02/arab-republic-of-egypt-technical-assistance-report-public-investment-management-assessment-547051)**, IMF, 2024-04-02. Claim: The IMF describes concrete management reforms such as better appraisal, procurement, portfolio management, and transparent budget reporting; this supports a technocratic, rules-based reading, but it is process evidence rather than proof of political separation from personal networks. Question IDs: 7B.3.

- **[Promoting Inclusive Human Capital Development and Building Resilience in Egypt Through Cash Transfer Programs](https://www.worldbank.org/en/results/2024/05/28/promoting-inclusive-human-capital-development-and-building-resilience-in-egypt-through-cash-transfer-programs)**, World Bank, 2024-05-28. Claim: Takaful and Karama is described as institutionalized, well-targeted, and run with proxy means testing and grievance mechanisms; this is evidence for rule-based welfare delivery rather than obvious patronage. Question IDs: 7B.3.

- **[President El-Sisi Meets Prime Minister and Members of the New Government](https://sis.gov.eg/en/media-center/news/president-el-sisi-meets-prime-minister-and-members-of-the-new-government/)**, State Information Service, 2024-07-03. Claim: Sisi told the cabinet to strengthen institutional frameworks, coordination, integrity, and transparency; coupled with a technocratic reshuffle, this is a limited positive signal, but still official self-presentation. Question IDs: 7B.3.

- **[House of Representatives Approves Drafted Social Solidarity Bill](https://sis.gov.eg/en/media-center/news/house-of-representatives-approves-drafted-social-solidarity-bill/)**, State Information Service, 2024-12-01. Claim: The bill aimed to unify support programs and formalize eligibility rules for Takaful and Karama; that suggests more rule-based administration and less ad hoc distribution. Question IDs: 7B.3.

- **[Egypt - 2024 Investment Climate Statements](https://2021-2025.state.gov/reports/2024-investment-climate-statements/egypt/)**, U.S. Department of State, 2024. Claim: The report says SOEs and military-owned companies still enjoy significant advantages, including regulatory relief and tax exemptions, while private firms complain about inconsistent enforcement against state and military entities; this is strong evidence against a clean separation of public decisions from regime-connected economic interests. Question IDs: 7B.3.

- **[OECD Economic Surveys: Egypt 2024](https://www.oecd.org/en/publications/oecd-economic-surveys-egypt-2024_af900de2-en/full-report/component-8.html)**, OECD, 2024. Claim: OECD says wide state involvement crowds out the private sector, military-owned firms have tax and land/resource advantages, and ownership structures are opaque; this is among the clearest structural negatives for the lens. Question IDs: 7B.3.

- **[Egypt’s New Laws Entrench Military Power Over Civilians](https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/03/05/egypt-new-laws-entrench-military-power-over-civilians)**, Human Rights Watch, 2024-03-05. Claim: HRW says new laws expanded military power over civilians and gave the state tools to pressure businesses; this cuts directly against separation of state policy from military-economic interests. Question IDs: 7B.3.

- **[Egypt’s Sisi Names Ex-Defence Chief as Adviser After Reshuffle](https://www.yahoo.com/news/egypts-sisi-names-ex-defence-140545714.html)**, Reuters via Yahoo, 2024-07-03. Claim: Reuters reported that the outgoing defense minister and chief of staff were moved into presidential adviser roles, which looks like managed elite recycling rather than an open break from trusted insiders. Question IDs: 7B.3.

- **[Egypt’s Sisi Replaces Head of Powerful General Intelligence Agency](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/Egypt-s-Sisi-replaces-head-of-powerful-general-intelligence-agency-48090165/)**, Reuters via MarketScreener, 2024-10-16. Claim: The intelligence chief was replaced by his deputy, but the outgoing chief remained close to the presidency and the service stayed tied to domestic security and dissent control; that is evidence of continuity in a politically embedded security apparatus. Question IDs: 7B.3.

**Search gap:** I did not find reliable public evidence in 2024 of a named Sisi family business winning specific contracts, receiving licenses, or directing law-enforcement actions for private gain. The evidence base is mostly structural: military/state economic advantages, elite continuity in top posts, and reform intent that does not yet overcome entrenched connected-actor privilege.
